butter_curator.text: Welcome to the Butter Exchange. It opened in 1769. Butter was weighed, graded and branded right here, then packed in barrels.
In its day Cork was one of the biggest butter markets on Earth. Salted butter kept well, so ships carried it round the world.
A barrel of it was called a firkin. A Cork firkin held about 25 kilos, which is a lot of toast.
